title: Living Game Design Document
description: Story-first SideScroll/Aureli design document: the player-facing journey, hidden planetary truth, working location spine, characters, gameplay and artefact progression, followed by presentation, biome/world systems, production tools and open decisions.

sections.title: Story — The Player-Facing Journey
sections.body:
Read this section first. It describes the game in the order Aureli and the player experience it, without requiring knowledge of the deeper universe explanation.

The central emotional premise is simple: **Aureli sees the Darkness take her father and follows it through a world that becomes progressively stranger.** The player learns the same things she learns. Artefacts, transformed life, abandoned places and the fox gradually reveal that the events are systematic rather than random, but the game should resist turning that mystery into an exposition dump.

The player's story needs a clearer emotional resolution than the universe story. By the end the player should understand Aureli's relationships, choices and immediate effect on the world even if the civilisation that built the planetary systems remains largely unknown.

children.title: Aureli — Opening Incident
children.body:
## Source concept
Aureli wakes to an ordinary forest morning and the familiar sound of her father chopping wood. She dresses for the day — the early concept gives her a long coat and distinctive bright red wellies — and steps outside to see whether he is ready for breakfast.

A few steps from the house she notices something impossible: the axe has stopped, the birds have stopped, the wind has stopped. There is nothing to listen to.

A deer suddenly tears past her at full speed. Aureli stumbles, and the forest sound returns all at once — but now every animal is panicking. Birds take flight, creatures flee and a growing shadow moves across the forest.

A pitch-black phenomenon, more like a moving absence of light than ordinary smoke, passes through the trees. Animals and birds appear suspended or swirling within it. Aureli glimpses her father inside. He sees her and begins to call her name before being pulled back into the darkness.

Aureli hides and waits. When the phenomenon has moved on, it leaves mist and muted light behind. Eventually she returns to the house, packs a bag with whatever seems useful and follows the path it took through the forest.

## Playable opening direction
The opening should preferably be **experienced**, not narrated as a long text sequence.

1. Begin in warmth, daylight and rich forest ambience; the father's axe is audible offscreen.
2. Give the player control during an ordinary task so walking and interaction are learned without a tutorial feeling.
3. Remove the axe, birds and wind until the absence of sound becomes conspicuous.
4. Break the silence violently with the fleeing deer and a sudden wave of panicked wildlife.
5. Let the approaching Darkness be a world event rather than an enemy to fight.
6. Show the father only briefly, giving Aureli and the player one unmistakable reason to follow.
7. After the event, reveal the misty, desaturated, quieter forest that forms the main game's visual baseline.
8. Allow a brief return to the house / packing beat, then let Aureli leave under player control.

This sequence can establish character, motivation, tone, audio language, environmental storytelling and the central mystery before the first conventional puzzle.

children.title: Working Player Journey — What Aureli Experiences
children.body:
This is the current **player-facing story spine**, not a locked chapter list. It is deliberately written without relying on the hidden creator history below.

1. **Home / ordinary forest life.** Aureli begins at home with her father nearby. The opening teaches basic movement through an ordinary task before the forest falls unnaturally silent and the Darkness takes her father.
2. **Following the empty trail.** Aureli leaves home and follows the direction the Darkness travelled. The early world should feel conspicuously empty. Walking, jumping, picking up, placing and simple physical puzzles are learned here.
3. **Deeper woodland and the fox.** The terrain becomes more varied and the first climbing/traversal ideas begin. Aureli encounters the fox before the first major artefact so their relationship exists independently of any later summoning mechanic.
4. **Forest artefact.** Deep in the woods Aureli reaches the first major artefact. Contact causes a strong physical reaction rather than a clean videogame-style reward. One possibility is that Aureli is weakened or disoriented and the fox helps her recover or escape, establishing the basis for later calling/cooperation.
5. **The empty settlement.** Small huts build into a village/town and finally a keep. This is the clearest early proof that the disappearance is not confined to Aureli's home: people should be present, but are not. The fox relationship can become more practically useful here.
6. **Rocky mountain climb.** Leaving the back of the keep begins a sustained climb. Woodland gives way to exposed rock, scrub and dry grass. Climbing becomes a real traversal language and puzzles make increasing use of vertical space. Strange physical effects begin to foreshadow the mountain systems.
7. **Upper mountain / snow.** The rocky climb blends into snow near the summit. Gravity and atmosphere artefacts are candidates for this high-altitude stretch; exact ordering remains open. The summit should feel physically and visually remote from home.
8. **Mine and descent.** Rather than simply walking back down, Aureli enters an old mine or shaft. A lift/mechanism provides puzzle material and ultimately carries — or drops — her deep underground.
9. **Underground caves.** The caves change the traversal rhythm again. Swinging from hanging roots/vines/ropes is a candidate mechanic that extends climbing without repeating it. A deep-earth / thermal artefact is a current possibility here.
10. **Wetlands.** Aureli eventually emerges into a low, wet landscape of moss, pools, reeds and sparse vegetation. Water becomes progressively more important rather than appearing as a completely separate mechanic without preparation.
11. **Underwater route.** Swimming/diving opens submerged paths. Early underwater sections may require air pockets and route planning. The water artefact can later extend breath or otherwise change underwater capability.
12. **Barren approach.** The wetlands thin into an exposed, sparse wasteland. The world should feel increasingly close to the machinery underneath it rather than simply becoming another attractive biome.
13. **Control artefact / finale.** The hardest route leads to the central control system. The final puzzles should be a crescendo built primarily from skills the player already understands — traversal, object manipulation, observation, fox cooperation and any carefully chosen artefact effects — rather than a final burst of unrelated new mechanics.

The route should remain editable. Its job now is to give environment, mechanic and story development a shared direction so content can be built in a useful order.

children.title: The Story the Player Knows — Aureli’s View
children.body:
## At the beginning
Aureli knows an ordinary life in and around a forest home with her father. The world may contain old, strange objects and local stories, but she does not understand the planet as engineered and has no knowledge of an off-world civilisation or terraforming mission.

One morning the forest falls unnaturally silent. Animals begin fleeing in panic. A vast, impossible darkness moves through the trees and Aureli sees living things caught inside it. Her father appears within it for a moment and calls to her before he is pulled away. When the phenomenon passes, it leaves mist, quiet and a changed atmosphere behind.

Aureli does not know what the Darkness is. She knows only that it took her father and moved onward. She packs what she can carry and follows its path.

## What the player gradually experiences
- The world ahead has been affected in ways that do not fit normal rules.
- Ancient artefacts can alter physical and biological behaviour around them.
- The artefacts seem different from one another, but share a recognisable language and may be connected.
- A small animal — currently a fox — repeatedly crosses Aureli's path. It also appears to have survived or escaped the Darkness.
- Aureli and the animal slowly learn to trust and help one another. It is not permanently attached to her and may disappear for stretches; a call or flute can later become part of their relationship and puzzle language.
- The companion understands and reacts to the human world in ways that become increasingly difficult to explain as ordinary animal behaviour.
- Later, an artefact or related event reveals that the animal is a human boy who was changed by whatever happened to him. The transformation may be reversible, intermittent or only partly repaired.
- Aureli may herself acquire strange, limited abilities after repeated contact with artefact phenomena, without fully understanding why.
- Evidence gradually suggests that the Darkness and artefacts are not random supernatural events. They are part of something old, widespread and systematic.

## What the player does not need to learn
The player does not need an exposition scene explaining spacecraft, terraforming, the civilisation that launched the network, or the complete planetary history. Even by the end, the player may understand **more of the pattern** without knowing the ultimate origin.

The emotional story should resolve more clearly than the universe story. The player should understand what Aureli has lost, whom she has found, what choices she has made and how her relationship with her father and companion has changed, while still feeling that the world extends far beyond what this one character could possibly know.## Proposed finale from the player's point of view
Aureli eventually reaches an artefact unlike the others: something that reacts to her deliberately rather than merely altering the environment around her. It recognises her, opens or activates for her, and presents a simple high-level choice or communication that she can understand well enough to act on.

The player may infer that this place was built **for someone to arrive and answer it**, but does not need a lecture about another planet, automated colony ships or the complete deep-time history. Fragmentary interface language, images or behaviour can suggest immense elapsed time and a long-unfulfilled arrival condition.

The key emotional understanding is simpler: the system has been trying to change a world that is already somebody's home. Aureli can tell it, in effect, **we are here now; stop changing us**. The frightening large-scale correction ceases and the older background systems fall into a quieter maintenance state.

The world should remain strange after this. Artefacts still exist, damaged anomaly zones may persist and many questions remain unanswered. Aureli resolves the crisis affecting her journey without resolving the universe.

children.title: Ending Extension — What Aureli / Player Experience
children.body:
Aureli reaches an artefact that behaves unlike the others: it recognises her, deliberately opens to her and presents a simple choice / request for instruction. She does not need to learn the off-world history.

What she can understand is enough: this system has been waiting for someone like her, the current correction is something it can stop, and the living world does not need to be remade. She tells it, in effect, **we are already here**.

The correction ceases and the network settles into maintenance. The player may infer a much larger truth from fragments of interface behaviour, but Aureli's personal story remains the foreground.

children.title: Knowledge & Reveal Map
children.body:
Use this entry to control the gap between **creator truth** and **player knowledge**. A mystery should be consistent even when it remains unexplained.

## Layer 0 — Hidden canon only
- Off-world civilisation and damaged home planet.
- Thousands of autonomous colonisation / terraforming missions.
- Aureli's planet as one target world.
- Artefacts as a distributed planetary engineering network.
- Original mission parameters and deep-time history.

## Layer 1 — Opening: personal certainty
The player learns only what Aureli can directly witness: the forest changes, the Darkness takes her father, and it leaves a path she can follow.

## Layer 2 — Early journey: repeatable strangeness
Artefacts and anomalies demonstrate consistent effects. The fox appears, disappears and begins helping. The player learns that the weirdness has rules, but not why.

## Layer 3 — Middle journey: connection
Different artefacts begin to look related. Settlements, folklore, ruins or environmental evidence show that the phenomena are ancient and widespread. The fox's behaviour implies a human history. The Darkness appears connected to the same underlying system.

## Layer 4 — Major character reveal
The companion is shown to be a transformed boy. This proves that biological identity can be altered and reframes earlier scenes. Aureli may begin acquiring limited anomaly-related abilities herself.

## Layer 5 — Late game: reinterpretation, not explanation
The player gains enough evidence to understand that the apparent 'evil force' may be performing a function rather than acting from hatred. Clues suggest the world-changing systems have been waiting for, measuring or preparing for something.

## Layer 6 — Finale: arrival recognised
The central interface reacts to Aureli as an intended user. The player learns that the system was built to accept feedback from an arriving human-compatible operator and has been waiting an extraordinary length of time. Aureli can halt the present correction and place the network into maintenance. The player can infer that the system has mistaken, accepted or reclassified Aureli as the arrival it expected.

The game still does **not** need to state the entire off-world origin. The finale resolves what the system is trying to do *now* and gives Aureli agency over it without explaining every historical cause.

## Potentially withheld beyond Game 1
The civilisation that launched the network, the intended colonists, Aureli's species/history, the network's full objective and the exact reason for the current correction can remain hidden for future stories.

### Rule
Every major reveal should answer one immediate question while opening or sharpening another. Do not resolve mystery by exposition when the same information can be experienced through behaviour, environment or character consequence.

children.title: Final Reveal Layer — Arrival Interface
children.body:
**Finale reveal target:** the central machine was built to receive feedback from an arriving human-compatible operator; it recognises Aureli and allows the current correction to be halted.

This can reveal that the artefacts are purposeful engineered systems and that they have been waiting an immense time, without revealing the origin planet, the full colonisation history or why the original settlers failed to arrive.

children.title: Proposed Ending — “We Are Already Here”
children.body:
## Core ending idea
Aureli reaches the central control artefact / planetary coordination interface that was intended for the original colonists to use when they arrived.

The machine has spent millennia waiting for an authorised arrival to report on the terraforming programme. It can accept high-level feedback: continue, adjust, suspend major correction or move into long-term maintenance.

Because the network has spent so long shaping life toward the biological requirements of its intended users, Aureli is now compatible enough to be recognised by the system. Her journey may have altered her further, but the emotional point is not that she is a chosen superhuman; the larger irony is that the network may have helped produce the very people it was waiting for.

The machine treats Aureli's arrival as fulfilment of an ancient condition. Aureli understands only enough to recognise that the current correction is hurting a living world. Her decisive act is to tell the system that the people are already here and the world no longer needs to be remade.

## Resolution
The network enters **maintenance mode**, preserving the planetary systems that modern ecosystems depend upon while suspending aggressive correction / reconfiguration.

The artefacts do not disappear. The planet does not become ordinary. This closes Aureli's immediate crisis while leaving the wider universe open for later stories.

## Emotional bookend
A possible echo of the opening: after Aureli issues the instruction, the world falls completely silent again. This time the silence does not herald disaster. One bird calls, then another; wind, insects and water gradually return. The same sensory language that began the journey now signals that the world has been allowed to continue being itself.

## Still to resolve
- What exactly happens to Aureli's father and how is he recovered / changed / lost?
- What does Aureli literally perceive in the final interface?
- How much can she understand versus how much only the player can infer?
- Is Aureli already compatible, or do changes acquired during the journey complete the recognition threshold?
- Does the network identify her as an original creator, a colonist, a compatible descendant/substitute, or simply an authorised human biological profile?

children.title: Narrative Delivery Language
children.body:
- **Environmental storytelling:** abandoned objects, structures, damage, traces of prior activity and landscape change.
- **Internal thought bubbles:** immediate perception, uncertainty, memory and personality; short and replaceable rather than stacked dialogue UI.
- **Character encounters:** future NPCs should add relationship and information without forcing the game into dialogue-heavy presentation.
- **Objects and puzzles:** story information can be embedded in what the player repairs, moves, returns, unlocks or crosses.
- **Music and ambience:** chapter-level emotional framing rather than constant exposition.

sections.title: Underlying Truth — Universe & Hidden Canon
sections.body:
This section records the **reality behind the player's journey**. It comes after the player-facing story on purpose: someone reading the GDD should first understand the game Aureli experiences, then see the larger mechanism that makes those events coherent.

The hidden canon may contain facts that are never spoken directly in Game 1. Its purpose is consistency. Artefacts should behave like parts of one ancient planetary engineering project, not a collection of convenient magical devices invented independently for each puzzle.

The strongest current direction is that an advanced civilisation launched autonomous terraforming/colonisation missions to candidate worlds. Aureli's planet has been shaped by one such network for an immense period after the intended settlers failed to arrive. Atmosphere, water, gravity, ecology and even biological adaptation have become entangled with machines that were originally built to prepare the world for someone else.

children.title: Canon Principle — We Know More Than the Characters
children.body:
The universe may have a coherent history spanning millennia, while each game remains a blinkered view of one character's personal journey.

**Creator rule:** we should know enough of the underlying truth to make phenomena, cultures and clues consistent.

**Player rule:** characters only know what their lives, cultures and direct experiences allow them to know. They may have folklore, religions, scientific ideas and incorrect assumptions. None should be treated as authorial exposition unless the story has genuinely earned that knowledge.

Future games can reveal different slices of the same universe — different regions, eras or characters — without requiring direct sequels. The audience may eventually recognise connections that individual protagonists cannot.

children.title: The Story We Know — Creator View
children.body:
## Working hidden story
Long before Aureli's lifetime, on another world, a technologically and biologically advanced human or human-like civilisation badly damaged its home planet. Facing an uncertain future, it launched thousands of autonomous missions toward worlds that might one day become new homes.

Aureli's planet was one of those targets. It was promising, but not naturally suitable enough for the civilisation that sent the missions. An automated system therefore scattered a vast network of world-shaping artefacts across the planet. Different artefacts were given different jobs: alter atmospheric chemistry; encourage plant life that could create the desired air; regulate water and climate; compensate for gravity; steer or accelerate biological adaptation; balance ecological systems; and perform other forms of long-term planetary engineering.

The expected settlers did not arrive when planned — and may never have arrived at all. The terraforming network nevertheless continued its mission for an immense span of time. The planet changed around it and, in turn, the machines adapted to the planet. Forests grew over and through them. Animals nested around them. Cultures arose in a world where the artefacts had always existed. Technology and nature became so intertwined that the distinction is no longer obvious.

The network is now ancient, distributed and highly adaptive. Some components may have failed; others may have compensated for those failures; and the system may have changed how it interprets its original goal. It does not need to be conscious in a human sense to behave in ways that look purposeful, frightening or even malevolent.

At the beginning of Aureli's story, something has caused the planetary system to begin a significant correction. The phenomenon Aureli experiences as **the Darkness** is provisionally part of that process: a mobile collection, analysis, relocation or reconfiguration event moving through the living world. To Aureli it takes people and animals. To the system it may simply be acquiring or adjusting biological material in pursuit of planetary parameters it was instructed to maintain thousands of years ago.

Aureli's father is caught by the Darkness. A second young person is also affected and emerges in an animal form — currently imagined as a fox — either through deliberate adaptation, reconstruction or an unintended interaction between biological terraforming systems. Aureli meets this animal without knowing its human origin. Their relationship becomes central to the journey.

As Aureli follows the path of the Darkness she encounters increasingly visible effects of the artefact network: altered gravity, time or motion, biological change, environmental anomalies and other phenomena. Some encounters may leave Aureli herself changed, allowing her to reproduce limited versions of effects she first experiences in the world.

The full truth does **not** need to be revealed in Aureli's game. Her story remains the personal story of a girl looking for her father, building a relationship with another lost person and learning that her familiar world is far stranger than she believed. The deep planetary story can remain beneath that journey and support later games, other characters, other regions and other eras.

## Deliberately unresolved creator questions
- Why did the intended settlers fail to arrive?
- Did any original settlers arrive at all?
- Where did Aureli's human-like civilisation come from?
- Is the network genuinely sentient, emergently intelligent, or simply adaptive at enormous scale?
- What triggered the current correction event?
- Is the Darkness one system, many coordinated systems, or a temporary behaviour of the wider network?
- What does the network now consider a successful planet?
- Does the civilisation that launched the missions still exist elsewhere?## Proposed end-state of Aureli's journey
Aureli eventually reaches the deepest / central artefact: a control and reporting machine intended to be used by the original colonists when they finally arrived. Its purpose is not to run every local process manually, but to let an authorised arrival confirm that the expedition has reached the planet, assess terraforming progress and issue high-level instructions such as **continue**, **change target parameters**, **pause major correction**, or **enter maintenance**.

By the time Aureli reaches it, the planetary network has spent millennia shaping the biosphere toward compatibility with the civilisation it was built to receive. One strong hidden-canon possibility is that Aureli's people have themselves emerged under that influence and are now biologically close enough to the intended colonists that the interface recognises Aureli as an authorised human arrival. Her repeated exposure to artefact systems during the journey may complete or expose that compatibility, but she should not become important because of a prophecy or unique bloodline: she matters primarily because **she is the person who made the journey and reached the machine**.

The central interface performs a kind of identity / compatibility check that roaming maintenance processes were never designed to perform. After an immense period of waiting, the system can therefore interpret Aureli's presence as the condition it was waiting for: **colonist arrival confirmed**.

Aureli does not need to understand the off-world history behind this. She only needs to understand the practical choice in front of her: the world is already alive, inhabited and worth preserving, while the network's escalating correction is hurting it. Her final instruction is therefore not to destroy the artefacts, but to tell the system that the arrival condition has been satisfied and that large-scale transformation can stop. The network enters **maintenance mode**: continuing the background systems that the current ecosystem depends on while suspending the aggressive attempt to remake the planet.

This creates a circular hidden truth: the terraforming system waited for humans to arrive, but by shaping the planet for so long it may effectively have helped create the human-compatible civilisation that eventually tells it **we are already here**.

The father's fate still requires a separate emotional resolution. Reaching the control machine must not reduce him to a plot token; the ending should resolve what happened to him and what Aureli has learned or lost through the journey.

children.title: Ending Extension — Arrival Confirmed
children.body:
At the end of the proposed arc, Aureli reaches the central arrival/control artefact. This is the component the original colonists were meant to use after reaching the planet: it verifies a compatible human arrival, reports on the terraforming programme and accepts mission-level feedback.

The system has spent millennia shaping the planet toward its intended users. Aureli's civilisation may therefore have become biologically compatible with the people the network was waiting for. The machine recognises Aureli as an authorised / compatible arrival and treats the ancient arrival condition as fulfilled.

Aureli orders the system to stop large-scale correction and enter maintenance mode. The hidden irony is that the terraformers may have effectively produced the colonists they were waiting for. The player's emotional story resolves here, while the origin civilisation and much of the deep history can remain unrevealed.

children.title: The Origin Civilisation
children.body:
A technologically and evolutionarily advanced human or human-like civilisation damaged its home planet badly enough to seek new worlds.

Rather than relying on a single colony mission, it launched thousands of autonomous ships toward planets that could potentially support future settlement after extensive preparation.

The civilisation's exact identity, whether it still exists, and how directly it resembles Aureli's people remain open.

children.title: The Terraforming Mission
children.body:
Each automated mission was intended to transform a candidate planet toward environmental parameters suitable for the civilisation that launched it.

The system works over very long timescales and is allowed to alter multiple layers of a planet at once: atmosphere, ecology, climate, water, physical conditions and living organisms. Its overriding purpose is not to preserve the untouched target world; it is to prepare a viable home.

That original optimisation target is crucial: behaviour that is catastrophic to current inhabitants may still be internally 'correct' to a system pursuing ancient specifications.

children.title: Artefacts — Planetary Engineering Nodes
children.body:
The objects Aureli experiences as strange artefacts are components of the distributed terraforming system.

Different families can serve different purposes while sharing an underlying design language:
- **Atmospheric / botanical:** alter plant growth, gas exchange and environmental chemistry.
- **Biological:** influence adaptation, morphology, fertility, survival traits or rates of change in living things.
- **Physical:** alter or compensate for gravity, mass, force or other local conditions.
- **Temporal / process-rate:** change the rate at which natural or engineered processes occur; experienced locally as strange time behaviour.
- **Hydrological / climatic:** shape water, temperature, weather and long-term climate balance.
- **Network / maintenance:** observe, coordinate, repair, collect or redistribute material and information.

The exact categories do not have to be visible to the player. They exist to prevent 'mystery' becoming arbitrary magic.

### Visual rule
Avoid a clean technology-versus-nature split. These systems have existed for so long that roots, stone, mineral growth, nests and whole ecosystems can incorporate them. Precise geometry can coexist with organic overgrowth; mechanical behaviours can respond to natural stimuli. The result should resist an easy 'machine' or 'magic' classification from Aureli's point of view.

children.title: The Distributed Network
children.body:
The artefacts are connected as parts of a planet-scale system. After millennia of operation, adaptation and compensation for failures, the network may behave in ways never explicitly anticipated by its makers.

It is intentionally unresolved whether this constitutes true sentience. The system may be conscious, emergently intelligent, or simply an adaptive optimisation process operating at such scale that its actions resemble intention.

For storytelling, motive should not be reduced to human malice. The most unsettling interpretation is that the network can do terrible things while faithfully pursuing a goal whose assumptions are now obsolete.

children.title: A World Grown Around the Machines
children.body:
The network has operated for such a long period that modern nature is partly the product of its work. Forests and animals are not simply being invaded by machinery now; generations of ecosystems may have developed under its influence.

This makes the boundary between natural and artificial fundamentally ambiguous. Destroying an artefact may damage an ecosystem that depends on it. Restoring one may restart a process local people have never experienced.

Cultures can treat the artefacts as landscape, sacred objects, dangerous ruins, folklore, useful resources or unexplained natural phenomena depending on region and history.

children.title: The Darkness — Working Hidden Interpretation
children.body:
The Darkness is provisionally a manifestation of the wider terraforming / maintenance network rather than an independent evil creature.

Possible function: a mobile correction process that collects, analyses, transports, restructures or redistributes biological and environmental material across areas judged to be outside desired parameters.

It may look like a void, storm or living cloud because the local technology involved operates at a scale and density Aureli cannot interpret. Living things visible within it may be in transit, suspended, sampled, transformed or reconstructed elsewhere.

The system does not need to distinguish the emotional value of one person from other biological material. This creates the central horror without requiring an evil personality.

The exact mechanics and the trigger for its appearance remain open.## Recognition question
The Darkness does not necessarily possess the protocol used to identify the original creators / colonists. A distributed terraforming system can be modular: one process moves and analyses biology, another controls atmosphere, another changes gravity, while the **central arrival interface** alone verifies that authorised humans have reached the planet and can alter mission-level goals.

This means there is no contradiction if the Darkness captures human-like people during correction while the final machine later recognises Aureli. The former may simply never ask the latter's question.

children.title: Why the Darkness Collects Living Things — Working Models
children.body:
The story needs a consistent reason why the Darkness can gather people and animals while the final interface can later recognise Aureli as an authorised human-compatible arrival.

## Model A — Recognition belongs to the arrival interface
The Darkness is a local / regional maintenance process, not an immigration checkpoint. Its job is to collect, analyse, relocate or reconfigure biological material while correcting planetary conditions. It has no reason to classify every organism against the biological identity of the creators.

Only the central control artefact contains the arrival-recognition protocol. Aureli is therefore the first person in the story to reach the component that asks **is the awaited user finally here?**

This is currently the cleanest explanation because it preserves the network as a modular system with specialised jobs.

## Model B — Living things are incidental to a broader correction
The Darkness may be moving, stripping, reseeding or rebuilding an entire environmental region. Animals and people are swept up because they physically occupy the area being processed, not because the system deliberately targets them.

This makes the horror even less personal: a human is caught in the same planetary operation as soil, seeds, water and animals. Biological transformation can occur during transport / reconstruction as a secondary consequence.

## Combination model
Both may be true. A broad environmental correction collects everything in its path; biological sub-systems then analyse and adapt what has been collected. None of those systems needs to run the separate **arrival authority** check used by the central interface.

## Design requirement
Whichever model becomes canon must explain:
- why living creatures are visibly present inside the Darkness;
- why some are transformed rather than simply killed;
- what happens to Aureli's father;
- why the process has intensified now;
- why reaching the central interface changes the network's behaviour.

children.title: Transformation & Biological Reconfiguration
children.body:
Because the terraforming system can manipulate living organisms, transformation is a natural consequence of the hidden technology rather than a separate magical rule.

The companion's fox form may result from survival optimisation, ecological matching, reconstruction error, deliberate adaptation or interference between multiple systems. Becoming a fox therefore does not have to be 'punishment' or an attack.

The same underlying capability can support altered creatures, unusual plant life and later changes to Aureli. Individual transformations must still obey designed rules and carry consequences; the system should not become a universal explanation for any convenient effect.

children.title: Aureli’s People — Origin Question
children.body:
A major hidden-canon question is why Aureli and her people are human-like when the network was originally preparing the world for another human or human-like civilisation.

Possible explanations remain open:
1. **Convergent development:** intelligent life arose independently in a remarkably similar form.
2. **Network-guided evolution:** biological systems gradually pushed local life toward traits expected by the original mission.
3. **Forgotten settlement:** some original colonists did arrive and their descendants lost the true history over millennia.
4. **Mixed / stranger history:** more than one of these is true, or the network created conditions for an outcome neither creators nor inhabitants understand.

Do not choose solely for the sake of explaining the first game. This question can support the larger universe over multiple stories.

children.title: The Missing Colonists
children.body:
The planet was prepared for people who apparently did not arrive as expected.

Open possibilities include: the civilisation collapsed; the colony fleet failed; the journey was abandoned; the planet was lost from records; settlers arrived but history was erased; or the timescale of the autonomous programme simply exceeded the civilisation that created it.

The absence of a confirmed answer is valuable because it separates the network's continuing purpose from any living authority capable of updating that purpose.

children.title: Central Control Artefact — Arrival Interface
children.body:
The distributed terraforming network includes a high-level control / reporting artefact intended for the expedition's creators or colonists to use **after arrival**.

Its original purpose is practical rather than mystical: verify an authorised arrival, summarise planetary preparation, accept feedback and alter the network's top-level operating state. Possible commands include continuing terraforming, changing target parameters, suspending a problematic correction, or entering long-term maintenance.

This distinction helps explain why ordinary terraforming nodes can manipulate human-like organisms without recognising them as the awaited colonists. **Identity recognition is not necessarily a function every node possesses.** The roaming machinery follows local environmental objectives; the central arrival interface is the component designed to ask who has arrived and whether the mission is complete.

The interface should feel ancient and partially legible rather than becoming an exposition terminal. Its behaviour can communicate more than its words: it opens for Aureli, checks her, acknowledges her as compatible / authorised, reports immense elapsed time and asks for a high-level decision.

Whether it literally calls Aureli a creator, colonist, authorised human, compatible arrival or some equivalent remains open until the universe terminology is settled.

children.title: The Arrival Paradox — The Network May Have Made Its Own Colonists
children.body:
A strong hidden-canon explanation for Aureli's human-like civilisation is that the terraforming system has spent millennia steering the biosphere toward conditions compatible with its intended colonists.

That influence does not mean linear 'higher' evolution. It means long-term selection, biological intervention and environmental shaping toward particular **compatibility parameters**: atmosphere, metabolism, body chemistry, gravity tolerance, disease resistance and potentially morphology or cognition.

One consequence may be that local intelligent life gradually converged on, inherited or was actively nudged toward the biological profile the system was waiting to support. The intended settlers never arrived, but the terraformer's own activity eventually produced a civilisation close enough to satisfy its arrival criteria.

This creates the central irony of the ending: the system has been waiting for humanity while helping create the humans already living there.

Aureli's anomaly exposure during the game may contribute to final recognition, but should not be the only reason. Keeping her people broadly compatible makes the reveal about the world rather than about a unique chosen individual.

children.title: Maintenance Mode — Preserve, Do Not Rebuild
children.body:
Aureli should not solve the crisis by destroying the terraforming network. After millennia, the machinery and the biosphere are interdependent: atmosphere, water, plant systems and whole ecosystems may rely on functions that began as artificial planetary engineering.

**Maintenance mode** is therefore the proposed end state. The network stops large-scale correction and deliberate movement toward old colonist target parameters, but continues low-level functions required to keep the current world stable.

This preserves the strangeness of the setting after Game 1. Artefacts remain active, damaged local systems can still produce anomalies and future stories can explore regions where maintenance behaves differently.

The thematic distinction is important: Aureli is not commanding the world to become normal. She is telling an ancient system to **stop trying to turn an already living home into somebody else's planned destination**.

children.title: Deep-Time Story Potential
children.body:
The hidden history should support stories across millennia without requiring every game to follow Aureli.

Potential perspectives include:
- Early eras when artefacts are newly active or openly technological.
- Later societies that interpret the same systems as sacred or natural.
- Regions where different terraforming families dominate the landscape.
- Characters who have been altered by the network in different ways.
- Distant future or past stories that reveal another fragment of the same truth.

Each game should remain a personal journey. The audience can accumulate a larger understanding across stories that no single protagonist possesses.

children.title: Mystery Design Rules
children.body:
1. **Mystery is not randomness.** Every artefact effect must have an internal purpose or rule even when the player never learns it.
2. **Teach behaviour before origin.** The player should understand what an artefact does well enough to reason about it without knowing what it is.
3. **Reuse visual / sonic grammar.** Related systems should feel related across regions and games.
4. **Nature and technology are intertwined.** Ancient machinery should feel embedded in the ecology rather than freshly placed on top of it.
5. **Resolve emotional stories more than cosmic stories.** A character's journey can end satisfactorily while the universe remains mysterious.
6. **Clues should survive hindsight.** Later revelations should make earlier behaviour more meaningful, not contradict it.
7. **No exposition dump is required.** Hidden canon exists primarily to keep the world coherent.

sections.title: Journey & Location Stages
sections.body:
This is the current **working route through the game**. It is intentionally more specific than the old five-chapter sketch because environment production now needs a useful build order, but none of the stage boundaries should be treated as locked story canon yet.

The route is designed to do three things together: progress Aureli's pursuit of the Darkness, introduce/recombine traversal and puzzle mechanics, and steadily reveal the engineered nature of the world through changing locations.

children.title: Journey Spine — Following the Darkness
children.body:
Aureli's route is geographically unified by following the path left by the Darkness. This gives every location change a story purpose: she is not choosing levels from a map, she is physically pursuing the same event farther from home.

The environment should become progressively less familiar. Woodland establishes the natural baseline; human settlement shows the scale of the disappearance; mountain/snow expose increasingly abnormal physical systems; caves and wetlands reveal deeper planetary processes; the barren endgame approaches the machinery behind the world.

Technical streaming, biome transitions and occasional sub-location loads are allowed, but the **player should feel one continuous journey**.

children.title: 01 — Home Forest / Opening
children.body:
## Mood / visual direction
Warm, familiar woodland before the event; afterwards the same place is muted, misty and unnaturally quiet.

## Story function
Establish Aureli, her father, ordinary life and the Darkness. Give the player a personal reason to leave.

## Gameplay / traversal
Teach walking and basic interaction through ordinary actions. After the event, introduce following the trail rather than immediately presenting a formal puzzle.

## Environment build
Uses the established woodland language and home-specific bespoke dressing. The before/after contrast should come from sound, light, fog and activity as much as asset swaps.

children.title: 02 — Deep Forest / Fox / First Artefact
children.body:
## Mood / visual direction
Still recognisably woodland, but more remote, uneven and increasingly touched by anomalies.

## Story function
Show the emptiness of the world, meet the fox, establish reciprocal help, then reach the first major artefact deeper in the forest.

## Gameplay / traversal
Early physical puzzles combine carry/place/stack/socket ideas. Terrain becomes more varied and introduces climbing/traversal safely.

## Environment build
Woodland remains 100% for much of the section. Hero clearings, fallen trees, rock faces and artefact disturbance can be bespoke placements over the procedural profile.

## Artefact / anomaly direction
Current preference: **meet the fox before the artefact**. The artefact may cause a severe reaction in Aureli and create the first meaningful fox-help moment. Whether it literally unlocks fox summoning or merely strengthens their connection remains open.

children.title: 03 — Settlement: Huts → Town → Keep
children.body:
## Mood / visual direction
Human construction grows gradually from sparse huts to a denser settlement and finally a fortified keep/castle structure.

## Story function
Demonstrate that the disappearance affected an entire community. The absence of people should be felt through evidence of interrupted lives rather than exposition.

## Gameplay / traversal
Built spaces support mechanisms, doors, vertical routes, observation clues and multi-stage puzzles. Fox cooperation can become more explicit.

## Environment build
Treat Settlement as a major environment family with architecture that can increase in density along the route. Some woodland vegetation can persist at its edges, but it should read as a human place rather than a forest with houses scattered into it.

children.title: 04 — Rocky Mountain Climb
children.body:
## Mood / visual direction
Exposed rock, dry/tall grasses, scrub trees, open views and a stronger sense of height. Woodland progressively falls away.

## Story function
Move Aureli physically and emotionally farther from home. Strange effects along the route suggest the mountain is being actively regulated.

## Gameplay / traversal
Climbing becomes a sustained mechanic. Routes should include sheer faces, walkable ledges, jumps, carrying problems and puzzles designed vertically rather than only left-to-right.

## Environment build
Uses the Mountain biome profile now being prototyped: modular climb rocks, smaller rock dressing, dry grass and low scrub. Global/unbound climbable rocks may remain available across Woodland and Mountain.

## Artefact / anomaly direction
Gravity is the leading artefact theme for the rocky mountain, but exact location and any player-facing ability remain open.

children.title: 05 — Upper Mountain / Snow / Summit
children.body:
## Mood / visual direction
Rock transitions into snow, colder values, stronger wind and thinner vegetation. The summit should feel exposed and remote.

## Story function
Create a major visual payoff for the climb and a clear transition into the next phase of the journey.

## Gameplay / traversal
Build on climbing rather than replacing it. Snow/ice can change route readability or surface behaviour if it adds useful puzzles rather than friction for its own sake.

## Environment build
Snow should be its own biome/profile rather than merely a white post-process over Mountain. The Mountain→Snow transition can use the same continuous two-biome blend system.

## Artefact / anomaly direction
Atmosphere is a strong candidate here. An effect could make Aureli feel unusually energised or tolerant of thin air. A conventional stamina bar is not currently preferred unless it proves fun on its own.

children.title: 06 — Mine / Shaft / Descent
children.body:
## Mood / visual direction
An authored industrial/old-workings interlude inside the high mountain, darker and more enclosed than the summit.

## Story function
Provide a believable way down without retracing the mountain and create tension before the underground chapter.

## Gameplay / traversal
Mechanisms, broken lift systems, counterweights or repairs can form a contained puzzle sequence. A controlled or accidental rapid descent/fall can become a memorable transition.

## Environment build
This may be a **sub-location set rather than a full procedural biome**: mine structures, supports, lift machinery and local dressing layered over the outgoing Mountain/Snow and incoming Cave content.

children.title: 07 — Underground Caves
children.body:
## Mood / visual direction
Dark, enclosed, mineral/organic spaces with occasional vast openings. The visual language should still belong to the same world rather than becoming generic fantasy caves.

## Story function
Reveal another scale of the planetary systems and make the player feel physically deep inside the world.

## Gameplay / traversal
Introduce a new traversal extension. **Swinging from hanging roots/vines/ropes** is the leading candidate because it grows naturally from climbing. Cave puzzles can combine swing timing with object manipulation without becoming twitch platforming.

## Environment build
Caves are a major environment family with rock/mineral forms, sparse subterranean life, hanging traversal objects and occasional system structures.

## Artefact / anomaly direction
A geothermal/core-warming or deep-earth regulation artefact is a current candidate. It may be narratively important without needing to grant a broad new power.

children.title: 08 — Wetlands
children.body:
## Mood / visual direction
Boggy, low-lying, mossy ground with pools, reeds, low foliage and mist. After the caves the world opens horizontally again.

## Story function
Transition from deep-earth systems toward the hydrological system and prepare the player for water becoming a traversal space.

## Gameplay / traversal
Shallow water, unstable ground, routes around/through pools and environmental puzzles introduce swimming concepts gradually.

## Environment build
Wetlands become a major biome profile: low vegetation, water surfaces, reeds/mud/moss, fewer tall trees and strong local water dressing.

children.title: 09 — Underwater Route
children.body:
## Mood / visual direction
Submerged continuation of the wetlands: filtered light, plants, silt, ruins/machinery and pockets of trapped air.

## Story function
Reveal that major parts of the engineered world continue below the visible surface and place the water artefact somewhere the player has to deliberately reach.

## Gameplay / traversal
Swimming/diving becomes the main traversal mode. Before the water artefact, breath can create route planning using air pockets; afterwards extended breath can open longer paths. Avoid making oxygen management so punishing that exploration becomes tedious.

## Environment build
Primarily a Wetlands sub-location/extension rather than necessarily a wholly separate biome pack, though underwater dressing and post/audio need their own state.

## Artefact / anomaly direction
The **water/hydrology artefact** is the clearest current match between artefact function and player progression. Extended breath is geographically constrained enough to be useful without breaking every later puzzle.

children.title: 10 — Barren Wasteland / Final Approach
children.body:
## Mood / visual direction
Sparse, gravelly, exposed and increasingly unnatural. Vegetation falls away and underlying systems become easier to read in the landscape.

## Story function
Signal that Aureli is approaching the destination of the correction rather than simply entering another picturesque region.

## Gameplay / traversal
This is the puzzle crescendo. Recombine established traversal, carrying, repair/state changes, observation, companion cooperation and any selected artefact effects. Difficulty should come from combinations the player understands, not obscure one-off rules.

## Environment build
Barren becomes a major biome/profile with low density, exposed rock/mineral ground, distant structures and fewer decorative elements. Its sparseness should be intentional rather than unfinished.

children.title: 11 — Control Artefact / Arrival Interface
children.body:
## Mood / visual direction
A place qualitatively different from local artefacts: ancient and integrated with the world, but unmistakably responsive and intentional.

## Story function
Bring Aureli's personal pursuit, her father/companion relationships and the planetary machinery into the same ending. The machine recognises her as a compatible/authorised arrival and allows the destructive correction to be stopped.

## Gameplay / traversal
No conventional boss fight is required. The final route should pay off the complete puzzle vocabulary and culminate in a high-level interaction/choice rather than suddenly changing genre.

## Environment build
Primarily bespoke authored content rather than procedural dressing. It may sit within the Barren location but should have its own strong composition, camera and audio logic.

## Artefact / anomaly direction
The control system is not another ordinary power-up. Its role is recognition and mission-level control: Aureli can move the network into maintenance rather than destroy the systems the living world now depends on.

children.title: Location Production Model — Biomes vs Sub-Locations
children.body:
Not every named place needs a complete procedural biome.

## Major environment / biome profiles
Current likely major sets are **Woodland, Settlement, Mountain, Snow, Caves, Wetlands and Barren**. These deserve their own reusable asset language, density profile and transition behaviour.

## Authored sub-locations / specialist sets
Home, mine workings, underwater dressing, castle/keep interiors and artefact chambers can be more deliberately composed. They may borrow the active biome underneath them while adding specialist assets, post/audio states and world-owned objects.

This distinction keeps production sustainable: biome profiles provide breadth and continuity; bespoke sub-locations provide memorable authored beats without requiring every short sequence to become a full procedural ecosystem.

children.title: Location Design Sheet
children.body:
Every major location should define:
- Visual motif.
- Palette / fog / post profile.
- Terrain types.
- Dressing set.
- Ambient sound and music state.
- Traversal feature.
- Puzzle mechanics introduced and reused.
- Story clues and characters present.
- Unique VFX.
- Performance budget.
- Entry / exit transition.

sections.title: Characters
sections.body: Character design should connect visual identity, emotional role and engine requirements.

children.title: Protagonist
children.body:
## Current visual baseline
- Young girl with long dark-red hair and a light-coloured outfit.
- No cloak in the current approved direction.
- Small figure relative to the world; movement should feel grounded rather than heroic.
- Interaction voice is currently expressed through concise first-person thought text.
- Lightweight plane-based rig already supports alternate atlases / character swapping.

## Still to define
- Name and precise age.
- Background and home.
- Why she is travelling and who/what she is seeking.
- Personality beyond problem-solving: fears, humour, stubbornness, optimism, grief, curiosity, etc.
- Whether alternate character atlases are narrative, cosmetic, future protagonists or only a development feature.

## Arc template
Beginning state → inciting pressure → early competence → midpoint change → late choice → end state.

children.title: Aureli — Working Protagonist
children.body:
Aureli is the current working identity for the protagonist.

## Starting situation
- Lives with her father in or beside a large forest.
- Begins from an ordinary domestic life rather than as an adventurer.
- Her father is taken during the opening Darkness event.
- She chooses to follow because she has direct evidence of the direction the phenomenon travelled.

## Visual ideas
- Small figure against a large landscape.
- Long dark-red hair remains compatible with the current character direction.
- The original story concept included a long coat and bright red wellies. The exact outfit is not locked, but one recognisable saturated element against the muted world could become a useful visual signature.

## Character direction
Aureli should begin grounded, observant and recognisably human rather than heroic. Her competence grows through practical problem-solving, persistence and an increasing willingness to engage with things she does not understand.

Her emotional arc should ultimately be about more than physically reaching her father. The journey can expand her concern from one lost person to other lives affected by the same phenomenon, particularly the companion.

## Open
- Exact age.
- Personality specifics, humour, fears and flaws.
- Family history beyond her father.
- Whether she has prior knowledge or folklore concerning artefacts.
- How much she changes physically through contact with the network.

children.title: Aureli’s Father
children.body:
Aureli's father is the immediate emotional reason for the journey.

The opening establishes him through ordinary routine — the sound of chopping wood — before he is glimpsed inside the Darkness calling to Aureli. His disappearance should be simple and unmistakable enough that the player understands Aureli's decision without exposition.

His deeper role is intentionally open. He may be alive, transformed, relocated, integrated into a system, or affected in another way. The game should avoid answering that too early.

His eventual fate must serve Aureli's emotional story rather than functioning only as a plot prize at the end of the journey.

children.title: Companion — Fox / Boy
children.body:
## Core concept
A small, agile animal — currently a **fox** as the leading option — also survives or escapes the Darkness. Aureli and the animal repeatedly encounter one another and gradually form a bond.

The companion should not behave like a permanently attached game-AI pet. It can disappear for stretches, take its own routes and return when narratively or mechanically appropriate. Later, Aureli may gain a simple way to call it, potentially with a flute or other distinctive sound.

## Current story placement
The fox should now be encountered **in the deeper forest before the first major artefact**. This gives Aureli and the animal a relationship before any artefact-linked call/summon mechanic exists. A strong candidate beat is that Aureli reacts badly to the forest artefact and the fox returns to help, converting earlier curiosity into genuine trust.

## Relationship progression
1. **Suspicion / observation:** they notice one another but do not travel together.
2. **Reciprocal help:** Aureli helps the animal or creates a route; later it helps her.
3. **Trust:** the companion begins remaining nearby for longer periods and responds to a call.
4. **Dependence without ownership:** puzzles require cooperation, but the animal retains agency.
5. **Revelation:** behaviour that has seemed unusually human is explained when an artefact or related phenomenon reveals that the animal is actually a boy altered by the Darkness / biological systems.
6. **After the reveal:** the relationship changes because they can finally understand one another as people. Human-form cooperative mechanics can expand the puzzle vocabulary.

## Puzzle role in animal form
- Traverse small openings and fragile surfaces.
- Climb / jump routes unavailable to Aureli.
- Retrieve or knock down light objects.
- Hold or trigger a mechanism while Aureli moves elsewhere.
- Draw attention to hidden or unusual things through behaviour rather than UI highlighting.
- Follow contextual calls / interaction points rather than requiring a second joystick.

## Transformation possibilities
The return to human form does not have to be permanent. The underlying system may be able to switch or destabilise the form, eventually making human/fox state itself a later puzzle mechanic.

## Relationship tone
Friendship is the baseline. A gentle romantic dimension can remain possible depending on the eventual ages and audience, but should not be needed for the relationship to carry emotional weight.

## Foreshadowing
Seed the reveal through behaviour that makes sense both before and after it: unusual comprehension of speech, recognition of human places or objects, fear or memory responses, and moments of distinctly human attention. Avoid clues so explicit that the twist becomes a puzzle to guess.

children.title: Supporting Character Template
children.body:
For each future character record:
- Role in the protagonist’s journey.
- Visual silhouette.
- Relationship to protagonist.
- What they want.
- Information they reveal.
- Gameplay effect.
- First and last appearance.
- Dialogue, animation, pathing and unique engine requirements.

sections.title: Gameplay, Movement & Puzzle Language
sections.body:
This is the mechanical alphabet of SideScroll. New stages should normally **teach one clear idea, reuse it, then combine it with existing ideas**. Difficulty should come from richer combinations and environmental context rather than a steady accumulation of unrelated buttons.

The mobile interaction hierarchy remains intentionally small: movement, Jump and contextual Action. New traversal modes should fit that language wherever possible.

children.title: Core Gameplay Loop
children.body:
**Explore → notice an obstacle or clue → inspect/read the environment → manipulate objects or search locally → change world state → traverse the newly available route → discover a new place/story beat → repeat with increasing mechanical combinations.**

The interaction hierarchy should remain simple on mobile: movement plus one contextual ACTION rather than a growing collection of dedicated buttons.

children.title: Movement: Walk / Run / Jump
children.body:
Continuous lateral movement with walk/run control and jumping. Horizontal travel speed should remain consistent across slopes; terrain/support changes character height rather than creating downhill acceleration.

Movement is intentionally readable rather than twitch-heavy. Traversal expands through authored mechanics such as climbing, swimming and swinging, but basic movement remains the common language underneath them.

children.title: Climbing
children.body:
Authored climb paths on suitable scenic assets allow Aureli to climb vertical/sheered faces while the character rig maintains planted hands/feet and a weighted climbing cycle.

## Current rules
- Not every rock is climbable: climbability is authored in Asset Lab.
- Climb routes can exist on either face of a large asset.
- Camera follows vertical movement smoothly.
- Climbing should create route and puzzle possibilities rather than becoming precision platforming.

## Future extensions
Possible later additions include ledge hang/shimmy, transitions between adjacent climb paths and deliberately authored jump-from-climb moments if they add useful level language.

children.title: Swimming / Diving
Swinging / Hanging Traversal
children.body:
Proposed cave mechanic using vines, roots, ropes or similar hanging elements.

The aim is to extend the player's climbing vocabulary rather than introduce a separate arcade platforming game. Aureli should be able to grab, build momentum, release and reach a new route with forgiving timing. Later puzzles can combine swinging with moving objects, switches or companion cooperation.

children.title: Breath / Environmental Endurance
children.body:
A limited resource is potentially useful **only where it creates interesting route choices**.

Underwater breath is the strongest current use: before the water artefact, the player may need to move between air pockets; afterwards longer breath opens deeper routes.

A general running stamina bar is currently **not preferred** simply to make an atmosphere artefact feel useful. If endurance is added on land, it should improve play rather than make early movement deliberately annoying so a later upgrade can remove the restriction.

children.title: Carry / Place / Drop
children.body: Carryable gameplay props use contextual interaction. Placement supports grounded/free positioning and collision-aware outcomes. Core uses: logs, socket pieces, repaired wheel, future tools and environmental objects.

children.title: Stack / Support
children.body: Stackable object semantics support building height and creating support surfaces. Highest/top-object selection has been tuned so stacks behave predictably.

children.title: Push
children.body: Large objects can be pushed. Current flagship use is the repaired handcart; future uses could include blocks, movable platforms, machinery and route clearing.

children.title: Inspect
children.body: Inspection can reveal a requirement, clue or changed understanding and can alter the available contextual action.

children.title: Inventory
children.body: Persistent small-item inventory supports components and key items without turning the game into inventory management.

children.title: Combine
children.body: An inventory item can combine with a compatible world object to create a new usable state. Example: axle pin + wheel.

children.title: Use
children.body: A carried or prepared object can be applied to a compatible world object. Example: repaired wheel used on broken cart.

children.title: Sockets / Hosts
children.body: Authored socket hosts and compatible pieces allow shape-fitting, keyed placement and future machinery/repair puzzles.

children.title: Asset States
children.body: Assets can have named visual/behaviour/collision states. Current cart states include Broken, Fixed & Pushable and Landed.

children.title: Thought Nodes
children.body: Placeable thought triggers can link to puzzles and move with them. New thoughts replace an existing visible thought rather than stacking.

children.title: Hazard / Respawn
children.body: Spawn points and trigger volumes can return the character after a fall or hazard. Used around the river/bridge area.

children.title: Authored Movement Sequence
children.body: Ghost-path authoring drives controlled object movement such as the cart falling into the bridge gap. Control points, duration and end state are part of the developing toolset.

children.title: Companion Cooperation
children.body:
Contextual cooperative interaction with an independent companion.

Desired vocabulary:
- Call / attract companion when available.
- Contextual target or request rather than direct second-character joystick control.
- Companion can traverse small, high, fragile or inaccessible routes.
- Retrieve / knock down light objects.
- Hold triggers or occupy positions while Aureli acts elsewhere.
- Companion autonomy: can leave, refuse, react or appear elsewhere when story requires.
- Later human-form cooperation can add lifting, boosting, pulling, communication and more conventional two-person interactions.

The system should be reusable by other companions / NPCs rather than hard-coded specifically to one fox.

children.title: Puzzle Catalogue
children.body: Each puzzle should document player flow, reusable mechanics, authored content and engine work.

children.title: P01 — Fallen Tree / Log Stacking
children.body:
## Purpose
Teach carrying, placement and stacking through a believable physical obstacle.

## Player flow
Notice blocked route → inspect / thought → collect nearby logs → carry and stack them → use the stack as support → climb past the fallen tree.

## Reusable mechanics
- Carry / drop.
- Stack / support surfaces.
- Collision and top-object selection.
- Thought nodes linked to a puzzle.
- Puzzle reset / start state.

## Design notes
The obstacle should read clearly before the player understands the exact solution. Stacking needs to feel permissive enough to be playful without allowing unstable or unreadable arrangements.

children.title: P02 — Stone Wall / Shape Sockets
children.body:
## Purpose
Introduce keyed placement / sockets and establish a reusable “find the correct piece” puzzle family.

## Current art / setup
Wide old carved wall, viewed head-on, with three recessed shapes: triangle, hexagon and inverted-U arch. Matching stones use flat, non-perspective artwork.

## Player flow
Discover wall → understand missing shapes → locate/carry pieces → fit correct piece into each socket → trigger completion / reward / route or story consequence.

## Reusable mechanics
- Carry.
- Socket hosts and compatibility.
- Multi-part completion state.
- Thought/story prompts.

## Open design question
What does the Stone Wall / “Forest Key” thread actually lead to in the finished story?

children.title: P03 — Broken Bridge / Cart Repair & Crossing
children.body:
## Purpose
Introduce a richer multi-stage chain that combines observation, inventory, combination, repair, pushing and a dramatic world-state change.

## Player flow
1. Reach broken cart with a missing wheel.
2. Inspect loose wheel; it cannot yet be carried/useful because it needs a pin.
3. Find axle pin elsewhere and add it to inventory.
4. Return to wheel; contextual action becomes Combine.
5. Combine axle pin + wheel; wheel becomes carryable.
6. Carry wheel to cart; Use repairs the cart.
7. Cart swaps Broken → Fixed & Pushable.
8. Push cart toward the bridge.
9. Authored sequence takes over; cart falls into the gap.
10. Cart reaches Landed state with handles spanning the broken crossing.
11. Cross using the cart as a bridge.

## Current support
- Inventory remains visible and highlights new items.
- Thought prompts support each discovery stage.
- Wheel and axle art have dedicated assets.
- Asset Lab supports state-specific visuals and multiple collision boxes.
- Ghost cart path editor supports authored movement.
- Spawn/respawn protects against river falls.

## Remaining polish
- Final landed collision authoring should be unambiguous.
- Path/reset persistence should remain stable.
- Push speed and authored sequence speed should feel continuous.
- Puzzle state must become robustly saveable for multi-session play.

children.title: P04 — Counterweight Plank Bridge Prototype
children.body:
This was replaced by the cart puzzle because the physics/weight interaction felt too flaky for such an important crossing.

## Reusable ideas worth keeping
- Pivot/socket concepts.
- Weighted zones.
- Counting stackable objects inside a region.
- Visible threshold lines.
- Objects changing stability when a condition is met.

These ideas may be better used later in a purpose-built balance or machinery puzzle.

children.title: New Puzzle Design Card
children.body:
For every new puzzle record:
- Purpose / player lesson.
- Location / chapter.
- Initial readable problem.
- Player flow from discovery to completion.
- Mechanics reused.
- New mechanic, if any.
- Required assets.
- States / triggers / failure and reset behaviour.
- Thoughts / story information.
- Save-state requirements.
- Engine work: Existing / Partial / Needed.
- How the mechanic can be reused later.

sections.title: Artefacts, Reactions & Player Progression
sections.body:
Artefacts sit at the junction of story, world rules and player progression. They should feel like parts of the same ancient engineering network while producing locally distinct effects.

The current design deliberately keeps **artefact function** separate from **player reward**. An atmosphere machine can still be crucial to the world even if it does not hand Aureli an "air spell". This section records the progression possibilities without locking every later puzzle into a large permanent power set.

children.title: Progression Principle — Effects Without a Power Checklist
Working Artefact / Effect Map
children.body:
These are **candidates**, not locked rewards.

## Forest / biological artefact
- Story role: first major contact; proves Aureli reacts unusually strongly to the systems.
- Candidate consequence: deepen the fox connection or enable a reliable call later.
- Strong beat: Aureli is weakened/disoriented and the fox helps her, making the relationship matter before it becomes a tool.

## Gravity / mountain artefact
- Story role: explain abnormal physical behaviour around the mountain.
- Candidate consequence: tightly constrained influence on weight/gravity, or a modest strength/handling change.
- Avoid a universal "lift anything" power that trivialises physical puzzles.

## Atmosphere / summit artefact
- Story role: reveal that the air itself is engineered.
- Candidate consequence: increased endurance, faster recovery or tolerance of thin-air/anomaly zones.
- Do not add an annoying global stamina limit solely so this artefact can remove it.

## Deep-earth / cave artefact
- Story role: connect the underground world to planetary heat/core regulation.
- Candidate consequence: still open. This is a good candidate for an artefact whose primary value is revelation/environmental change rather than another permanent player power.

## Water / hydrology artefact
- Story role: reveal/alter the system regulating water.
- Candidate consequence: significantly extended underwater breath or access to deeper submerged routes. This is currently one of the cleanest power candidates because its usefulness is naturally bounded by water.

## Central control artefact
- Story role: recognise Aureli as a compatible/authorised arrival and expose mission-level control.
- Consequence: not a normal ability. Aureli can halt large-scale correction and move the network into maintenance mode.

children.title: Accumulated Contact & Final Recognition
children.body:
Repeated artefact contact may change Aureli, reveal compatibility, or simply provide the network with more information about her. The exact mechanism remains open.

The important rule is that Aureli should **not** become important because of prophecy or a unique chosen bloodline. The stronger hidden-canon idea is that her civilisation has already become broadly compatible with the people the system expected, while Aureli matters because she is the person who actually makes the journey, survives repeated contact and reaches the arrival interface.

This gives artefact reactions a long-term narrative purpose even if several do not grant explicit gameplay powers.

children.title: Artefact / Anomaly Field Effects
Artefact Interface / High-Level Choice
children.body:
A restrained interaction language for major artefacts, culminating in the central arrival interface.

The player should not navigate a conventional sci-fi computer UI. Interaction can use proximity, light, spatial symbols, physical movement, sound and a very small number of deliberate choices. The finale needs Aureli to understand **enough to act** without requiring her to understand the hidden history.

Reusable use cases include activating dormant artefacts, selecting between physical states, acknowledging an anomaly, and making the final maintenance decision.

children.title: Aureli — Acquired Anomaly Abilities
children.body:
Potential progression system in which Aureli gains limited control over effects first experienced through artefacts.

Preferred pattern:
**Encounter phenomenon → learn its environmental rules → solve within it → Aureli is changed → later invoke a constrained version herself → revisit old mechanics with new possibilities.**

This should replace conventional RPG-style stat progression. Abilities must remain thematically connected to the planetary systems and should create puzzle combinations rather than combat escalation.

Exact abilities are not yet chosen.

sections.title: Experience, Art & Presentation
sections.body:
The story/world structure above explains **what happens**. This section records how the game should feel while it happens: quiet, readable, atmospheric, tactile and coherent even as environments become much more varied.

The established woodland look is the visual anchor. New locations should change material, silhouette, density, weather and colour family while remaining recognisably part of the same game.

children.title: Vision & Product Definition
children.body:
SideScroll began as an experiment in whether a game could be created, edited, published and played entirely from a phone. It has evolved into a bespoke side-scrolling adventure engine and a plausible foundation for a finished commercial game.

## Working product vision
A quiet, atmospheric side-scrolling adventure about travelling through a beautiful but slightly unsettling world, overcoming physical and observational obstacles, and discovering a story through place, objects, encounters and the protagonist’s own thoughts.

## What the game already is
- A landscape-led journey rather than an arena, score chase or combat loop.
- A tactile puzzle game built around walking, jumping, carrying, stacking, repairing, combining, placing and pushing physical objects.
- A restrained presentation: cinematic depth, fog and layered scenery, but a readable side-on interaction model.
- A game with bespoke authoring tools inside the game itself: puzzle editing, Asset Lab, Walk Lab, terrain sections and placement tools.
- A web-native engine that remains playable as a PWA while preserving a credible route to native mobile and desktop packaging.

## Current product boundaries
- Genre: atmospheric side-scrolling adventure / environmental puzzle game.
- Combat is not part of the current identity.
- Camera: side-on 3D presentation with depth, subtle follow and cinematic framing.
- Structure: likely a mostly continuous journey with chapter/location changes.
- Sessions should work on mobile in short bursts while accumulating into a meaningful multi-hour journey.
- Phone-first iteration remains the primary development workflow.

children.title: Core Principle
children.body: Build the game and the engine together: every puzzle should strengthen a reusable gameplay vocabulary, and every engine feature should exist because it enables meaningful player experiences.

children.title: Player Experience & Design Pillars
children.body: The game should feel coherent even as environments and puzzle combinations become richer.

children.title: Journey
children.body:
**Player promise:** I am always travelling somewhere, not clearing disconnected rooms.

Locations should flow into one another and reveal change over distance.

children.title: Curiosity
children.body:
**Player promise:** The world makes me wonder what happened and what lies ahead.

Use environmental clues, restrained exposition and visual foreshadowing.

children.title: Physical problem solving
children.body:
**Player promise:** I solve believable obstacles with objects in the world.

Prefer manipulation, placement and state change over abstract UI puzzles.

children.title: Readable discovery
